Why AI Chips Are Now Built Like Skyscrapers (with Dr. Benjamin Hein)
articles.description:
#Semiconductors #AIchips #Advancedpackaging 

In Episode #1045, Ben Hein (CEO of the Electronics business at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany) joins @JonKrohnLearns to explain how the chips behind the AI boom are actually made. His company is 358 years old, began as a pharmacy, and now supplies materials, systems and services across all six steps of semiconductor fabrication, a process of more than 1,500 steps that can take six months for a single chip. Ben succeeded Kai Beckman, who appeared on this show in Episode #875, and he has spent time in Taiwan and Boston on the way to the role. In this episode, he explains why performance per watt is the industry’s single biggest problem, why five decades of shrinking has given way to building upward, how AI-driven simulation lifted his R&D hit rate more than fivefold, and why he expects affordable high-quality healthcare in our lifetimes.

Interested in sponsoring a SuperDataScience Podcast episode? Email natalie@superdatascience.com for sponsorship information.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:07:18) The six steps of semiconductor fabrication
• (00:11:47) Why performance per watt is the industry’s biggest problem
• (00:17:30) How AI removes 85% of candidate molecules
• (00:26:31) Painting one wall on the 57th floor
• (00:42:48) Neuromorphic chips and the 20-watt brain

311: 10 Years of Manufacturing Happy Hour, Live from IMTS 2026
articles.description:
In 2016, manufacturing barely showed up on video. So Chris cracked open a beer and hit record on his iPhone.

Over 10 years, Chris has welcomed plenty of guests onto Manufacturing Happy Hour. For this anniversary episode, the roles are reversed. Jake Hall, Keynote Speaker and Industry Advocator at The Manufacturing Millennial, interviews him on the main stage at IMTS in Chicago, looking back on more than 300 episodes.

The conversation covers how the podcast grew from short videos in an automation lab to live tours and trade show stages. They discuss what makes a good guest, how manufacturing conversations have shifted since 2016, and what Chris would tell anyone thinking about starting a podcast.

In this episode, find out:

  • Why Chris believes leadership has nothing to do with job title
  • What a trip to Germany revealed about manufacturing challenges around the world
  • How to make your story stand out when everyone is talking about the same technology
  • Why Chris recommends starting a podcast with a 10-episode season
  • How a brewery collaboration led to Manufacturing Happy Hour's own IPA
  • Why podcast interviews should build trust, not turn into product pitches

Enjoying the show? Please leave us a review here. Even one sentence helps. It’s feedback from Manufacturing All-Stars like you that keeps us going!

Tweetable Quotes:

  • “The biggest thing is it helps me learn at the pace that the industry is going because I'm having these conversations weekly in real time.” - Chris Luecke, Podcast Host & Community Builder at Manufacturing Happy Hour
  • “You can go back for like over 100 years and look at newspaper clippings that say, ‘No one wants to work anymore.’” - Chris Luecke, Podcast Host & Community Builder at Manufacturing Happy Hour
  • “The more important thing is to get out there and share your voice on stages like this or even just pulling out your smartphone and recording a video.” - Chris Luecke, Podcast Host & Community Builder at Manufacturing Happy Hour

Links & mentions:

  • Stay Innovative, Stay Thirsty is a New England / Hazy IPA brewed by Amorphic Beer in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, in collaboration with Manufacturing Happy Hour.
  • Association for Advancing Automation (A3) is North America’s largest automation trade association, representing more than 1,500 organizations involved in robotics, AI, machine vision, motion control and related technologies.
  • The Association for Manufacturing Technology (AMT) is a trade association that supports the manufacturing technology industry through industry insights, business development, workforce initiatives, and advocacy.
  • The Manufacturing Millennial is Jake Hall’s platform advocating the future of robotics, automation, and manufacturing through keynotes, workshops, coaching, and events.
  • Made Here is Chris’s new TV series on RFD-TV, showcasing the people, companies, and communities shaping American manufacturing.

Make sure to visit http://manufacturinghappyhour.com for detailed show notes and a full list of resources mentioned in this episode. Stay Innovative, Stay Thirsty.
